papers.title: A Memorization Floor for LLM Refinement of Decompiled Code
papers.description: Studies whether LLM refinement of decompiled C recovers identifiers from input evidence or prior knowledge. Within-item ablations and output-matched chance baselines test naming gains on textbook and newly authored functions, including a second-model replication.

papers.title: Agentic Reverse Engineering: From I/O to Code with Discovery Agent
papers.description: Synthesizes executable programs from input/output observations using LLM-guided evolutionary search, progressively revealed examples, simple-to-complex mutations and execution-error feedback. An active variant chooses inputs and queries a hidden reference program.

papers.title: ASAP: Assembly-Source Aligned Pseudocode Refinement For Binary Decompilation
papers.description: ASAP aligns assembly and source representations during training, compresses assembly features into tokens, and supplies them alongside decompiler pseudocode to an LLM refiner. Masking and an assembly-advantage objective encourage the refiner to use low-level evidence.

papers.title: Automatically Attacking Software Reverse Engineering AI Agents
papers.description: A proof of concept for indirect prompt injection against Cline/GhidraMCP binary-analysis agents. An adapted AutoDAN generates embedded strings that make the agent describe different behavior. The authors demonstrate four small C programs with Qwen3-8B and transfer the examples to GPT-OSS-120B.

papers.title: Between the Commits: Process, Error, and Claim Reliability in a Wholly AI-Authored Codebase
papers.description: Studies development of the Extractor reverse-engineering tool through commits, available session logs and code-provenance tracing. Taxonomies separate instruction intent, change triggers and agent claims, exposing errors corrected before commits that ordinary repository history misses.

papers.title: Beyond Text Matching: Towards Reference-Free Evaluation for Human-Oriented Binary Reverse Engineering
papers.description: BinJudgeBench collects expert judgments for function naming, binary-code summaries and decompilation refinement. BinJudge learns to select a judge configuration for each input and task, evaluating agreement with human scores rather than executable correctness.

papers.title: Binary Decompilation LLM with Feedback-Driven Multi-Turn Refinement
papers.description: AutoDecompiler trains function-level decompilation models to revise assembly- or pseudocode-derived outputs using compilation, execution and I/O feedback. Its reinforcement-learning design combines diagnostic feedback with rewards for valid code, tested behavior, syntax and data-flow structure.

papers.title: CASCADE: LLM-powered JavaScript Deobfuscator at Google
papers.description: Uses Gemini to locate the prelude functions that Obfuscator.IO inserts for string obfuscation, then applies constant-propagation and inlining passes in the JSIR compiler IR to restore string literals and API names deterministically.

papers.title: CHISEL-ing Back Source Code with AI-enabled Iterative Recovery
papers.description: CHISEL refines Ghidra pseudocode using compiler diagnostics and type-aware differential fuzzing against the original function. It retains counterexamples and candidate history; existing I/O pairs are held out for evaluation rather than supplied to the recovery loop.

papers.title: CrackMeBench: Binary Reverse Engineering for Agents
papers.description: Evaluates agents on executable-checked CrackMe tasks: infer validation logic from binaries and submit an accepted input or artifact, while recording tool use, time, and scoring attempts.

papers.title: CREBench: Evaluating Large Language Models in Cryptographic Binary Reverse Engineering
papers.description: Benchmarks cryptographic binary reverse engineering across algorithm recognition, key or IV extraction, wrapper reconstruction, and flag recovery using 432 controlled challenges.

papers.title: Cyber-Zero: Training Cybersecurity Agents without Runtime
papers.description: Cyber-Zero synthesizes training trajectories for capture-the-flag (CTF) agents from public writeups instead of running the challenges. Writeups collected from CTFtime through the CTF Archives repository are cleaned, filtered and completed with DeepSeek-V3-0324, which fills in missing metadata and extracts flags; after removing 47 challenges that overlap the evaluation benchmarks, the corpus holds 6,188 writeups for 4,610 challenges from 543 competitions in six categories, 2017–2025. Two DeepSeek-V3-0324 personas then simulate each solve: a CTF player that sees only the challenge content, and a Bash terminal that sees the writeup and flag, invents plausible command output and may inject hints, which are removed before training. Trajectories use the EnIGMA scaffold format and are kept only if they reach the exact flag, pass format checks and are judged by an LLM filter to follow the writeup's approach. Qwen3, Qwen2.5-Instruct and SWE-agent-LM models are fine-tuned on 9,464 of these trajectories and evaluated with EnIGMA+, the authors' parallel version of EnIGMA, on InterCode-CTF, NYU CTF Bench and Cybench. The fine-tuned Qwen3-32B (Cyber-Zero-32B) rises from 20.3% to 33.4% average Pass@1, the 13.1-point gain reported in the abstract.

papers.title: Dashboard2Code: Evaluating Multimodal Models on Reconstructing Interactive Dashboards
papers.description: Evaluates agents that actively explore a running dashboard and reconstruct its appearance and interaction logic. DashboardMimic provides 180 Plotly+Dash examples, with code-semantic analysis and dynamic interaction tests for the generated implementations.

papers.title: Decaf: Improving Neural Decompilation with Automatic Feedback and Search
papers.description: Decaf samples multiple candidate decompilations, recompiles them and ranks them using compiler-derived byte distance or a learned reranker. The work studies candidate selection as a way to improve neural decompilation without an iterative source-repair conversation.

papers.title: Decoding What iOS Location Services Send to Apple: An LLM Is an Unreliable Analyst but a Useful Toolmaker
papers.description: Compares direct LLM recovery of Apple PBCodable schemas with an AI-written Extractor checked against compiled synthetic fixtures, published descriptors and captured traffic. It shows how plausible recovered schemas can silently decode values incorrectly.

papers.title: Decompiling Quantum Assembly into Structured Programs
papers.description: Quelle recovers library calls, loops, functions and symbolic parameters from compiled OpenQASM. It removes routing artifacts, proposes structured reconstructions and checks them against circuit semantics, retaining gate-level fallbacks when recovery fails.

papers.title: Decompiling the Synergy: An Empirical Study of Human–LLM Teaming in Software Reverse Engineering
papers.description: Studies how human analysts work with LLM assistance during static software reverse engineering. A survey of 153 practitioners informed six LLM features built into an instrumented IDA Pro plugin. Then 48 participants (24 self-reported novices and 24 experts) analyzed two CTF-style binaries, with the features enabled on one randomly assigned challenge. From graded writeups, interaction logs and surveys, the authors report 18 findings: novice understanding rose by about 98% to expert levels while experts gained little, known-algorithm functions were triaged up to 2.4× faster, and artifact recovery rose by at least 66%, alongside harmful hallucinations.

papers.title: Decoupling is a Necessity: Transformation-Agnostic Decompiled Code Recovery under Optimization and Obfuscation
papers.description: ReSource refines decompiled functions affected by compiler optimization and obfuscation. Its stages retrieve guidance from a Semantic Distortion Database, predict a control-flow skeleton, and refine names and formatting. Evaluation measures code similarity and retrieval of the corresponding original function from a source corpus.

papers.title: Does It Render Everywhere? A Study of Cross-Environment Compatibility in MLLM-Generated Webpages
papers.description: WebCompat evaluates screenshot-reconstructed webpages across browsers and devices. Its XCompat detector combines rendered DOM geometry, viewport metadata and screenshots to identify layout and element failures, independently of similarity to the original design.

papers.title: Echo: Learning-based Matching Decompilation using Trusted Back Translation
papers.description: Echo iteratively generates source and compiler configurations, recompiles candidates, and uses assembly differences to guide configuration search and code refinement. It evaluates matching on function benchmarks and selected functions from a Mirai binary.

papers.title: Faultless: A Program Equivalence Technique for Validating and Evaluating Neural Decompilers
papers.description: Compares neural-decompiler C output with deterministic decompilation or reference functions using symbolic execution and a specialized memory model. It supports both analyst-facing validation and model evaluation without requiring the surrounding codebase.

papers.title: FidelityGPT: Correcting Decompilation Distortions with Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.description: FidelityGPT post-processes existing decompiler output: an LLM labels lines with six distortion types, such as non-conventional dereferencing, redundant variables and confusing control flow, and then rewrites the labeled lines. Its prompts define the distortion types and add retrieval-augmented context from a manually annotated database of distorted IDA Pro and Ghidra lines. A semantic-intensity algorithm chooses which lines to query, and a variable-dependency analysis carries redundant-variable context across 50-line chunks. On 620 function pairs, the authors report 89% detection accuracy and 83% precision, and correction fix rates of 94% (FR) and 64% (CFR) against 83% and 37% for their DeGPT runs.

papers.title: FirmCure:Towards Autonomous and Adaptive Rehosting of Linux-Based Firmware
papers.description: FirmCure combines static dependency analysis, iterative boot-configuration repair and runtime fault diagnosis to rehost Linux firmware in QEMU. Specialized agents apply targeted repairs and use execution feedback to recover service behavior.

papers.title: FirmPilot: Evidence-Guided Multi-Agent Environment Recovery for IoT Firmware Rehosting
papers.description: FirmPilot reconstructs QEMU execution environments through coordinated retrieval, planning, filesystem, persistent-state and network recovery. Proposed changes are applied as constrained artifact deltas, then checked by rerunning the firmware and fixed probes.

papers.title: Fool Me If You Can: On the Robustness of Binary Code Similarity Detection Models against Semantics-Preserving Transformations
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE 2026)
papers.description: The paper builds asmFooler to test whether learned binary code similarity detection (BCSD) models keep matching functions after semantics-preserving changes. From 620 baseline x86-64 ELF binaries (coreutils, binutils, PuTTY, nginx, SPEC2006 and others, built with Clang at O0–O3), it generates 9,565 variants using in-place instruction rewriting, basic-block reordering, Obfuscator-LLVM, semantic NOPs and junk code, and it adds a greedy search for dead-code sequences that make dissimilar functions look similar. Across Genius, Gemini, Asm2Vec, SAFE, Trex and BinShot, robustness depends on each model's preprocessing, architecture and features: block reordering drops BinShot's recall from 0.972 to 0.036 but lowers it by under 0.05 for the CFG-based Genius and Gemini. The false-positive attack reaches up to 100% success with 14.75 inserted instructions on average.

papers.title: From Code to Requirements: Agentic Reverse Engineering of Business Rules at Enterprise Scale
papers.description: Uses seven agents and human review to recover business requirements from source, tests, configuration and documentation. A reported enterprise migration checks extracted rules against production-defect records.

papers.title: From Dead Code and Static Requirements to Working Engines: Software Revival with Coding Agents
papers.description: ReviveBench evaluates repair of nonrunning software and source-unavailable implementation of bounded computational and transactional engines from open specifications, using hidden reference-based checks. It also audits grading defects that can wrongly accept or reject reconstructions.

papers.title: From Obfuscated to Obvious: A Comprehensive JavaScript Deobfuscation Tool for Security Analysis
papers.description: JSimplifier recovers readable JavaScript from obfuscated scripts in three stages. A preprocessor normalizes malformed or mixed-encoding input; a deobfuscator combines AST-based static simplification with selective execution of obfuscated call sites in a Node.js vm context, feeding the results back into the AST; and an optional humanizer renames identifiers with an LLM, adapting HumanifyJS, then formats the output with Prettier. The authors catalog 20 obfuscation techniques in four categories and assemble MalJS (23,212 malicious scripts) and BenignJS (21,209 scripts). They report that JSimplifier processes all 44,421 samples and reduces Halstead length by 88.2% on 1,296 multi-technique JsDeObsBench samples.

papers.title: From Visual Widgets to UI Code: Efficient Tool-Grounded Generation
papers.description: WidgetGen reconstructs widget screenshots as React JSX. OCR text boxes and color palettes guide whole-widget layout reasoning and optional chart generation before one terminal render; generated render/code pairs also support model fine-tuning.

papers.title: GameReplica: A Benchmark for Black-Box Visual Game Replication by Vision-Language Agents
papers.description: Evaluates whether vision-language agents can infer hidden game rules through screenshots and active interaction, then build runnable single-file HTML replicas across 125 tasks from 25 web games, each with five difficulty levels.

papers.title: HELIOS: Hierarchical Graph Abstraction for Structure-Aware LLM Decompilation
papers.description: HELIOS gives an LLM a hierarchical summary of binary control flow and function calls alongside decompiler output, with optional compiler feedback. It evaluates compilability and functional correctness.

papers.title: Humans vs. Machines: A Comparison With AI Agents in Software Reverse Engineering
papers.description: Compares human and LLM-agent understanding and navigation on the same static reverse-engineering challenges, then studies how binary representations consume context windows.

papers.title: IChart2Code: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Interactive Chart Code Generation
papers.description: Benchmarks reconstruction of interactive charts from a reference screenshot, local data and specified actions. Its TRAIL framework uses Developer and Inspector agents with browser interaction traces to diagnose errors and revise the HTML/JavaScript implementation.

papers.title: Idioms: A Simple and Effective Framework for Turbo-Charging Local Neural Decompilation with Well-Defined Types
papers.description: Idioms fine-tunes code language models to turn Hex-Rays output for one target function into predicted original C together with definitions of the user-defined structs, unions and typedefs it uses. Input can include neighboring decompiled functions in breadth-first call-graph order, so evidence about a type scattered across callers and callees reaches the model. The authors also build Realtype, 157,163 functions from compiled open-source C repositories with full type definitions. Their CodeGemma-7b-based model passes ExeBench unit tests for 54.4% of functions versus 46.3% for LLM4Decompile and 37.5% for Nova, and scores at least 95% higher on Realtype.

papers.title: IWR-Bench: Can LVLMs reconstruct interactive webpage from a user interaction video?
papers.description: Tests reconstruction of interactive webpages from user-interaction videos and supplied static assets. Its 113 tasks replay annotated action sequences to assess visual fidelity and functional behavior across observed page states.

papers.title: Khost: KVM-based Near Native MCU Firmware Rehosting
papers.description: Extends KVM with MCU instruction handling, memory mapping and interrupt modeling to rehost firmware on ARMv8-A hosts. An MMIO monitor and firmware wrapper support peripheral interaction and coverage-guided testing.

papers.title: Lifting Optimized Binaries to Canonical Compiler IR via Structure-Aware Retrieval and Iterative Verification
papers.description: BRIDGE lifts stripped, optimized x86-64 and ARM64 functions, given as llvm-objdump disassembly, to LLVM IR. Its target is the unoptimized IR that a fixed clang -O0 configuration emits for the original source. Offline, it builds a retrieval database from 69,253 ExeBench functions compiled at -O0 to -O3, using LLVM pseudo-probe instrumentation to align assembly fragments with the matching -O0 IR regions. At inference it splits each function's angr-recovered control-flow graph into control-flow segments such as loops and if–else regions, retrieves the three nearest aligned assembly–IR pairs per segment from a FAISS index of Nova-1.3B embeddings, and prompts a hosted general-purpose LLM (DeepSeek-chat) to write the IR. Up to five refinement rounds then feed LLVM verifier and compiler diagnostics and unit-test failures back to the model. On HumanEval-Decompile and MBPP compiled with Clang 19 at -O0 to -O3, average re-executability is 65.2% and 65.4% on x86-64 and 45.6% and 42.1% on ARM64. The rule-based MCTOLL reaches 62.1% and 64.9% on x86-64, and the five directly prompted API LLMs reach at most 21.5%.

papers.title: LLM Agent-Assisted Reverse Engineering with Quantitative Readability Metrics
papers.description: Uses a composite Quantitative Readability Score (QRS) to guide agents refining decompiled C. Lexical familiarity, structural simplicity and coding idioms are combined with a binary-structure similarity gate. Experiments compare refinement with and without shell access on 210 simple C binaries.

papers.title: Locate, Then Reason: End-to-End Patch Presence Testing in Stripped Binaries
papers.description: Locates patch-relevant code in stripped binaries using instruction-aligned retrieval and caller/callee context, then uses an LLM to screen candidate matches and compare patch-specific behavior with vulnerable and patched references.

papers.title: MirrorCode: AI can rebuild entire programs from behavior alone
papers.description: Tests reimplementation of 25 command-line programs using execute-only reference access, documentation and visible examples. Separate scoring environments compare exact outputs on visible and held-out end-to-end tests.

papers.title: NotDec: WebAssembly Decompilation With Inter-Procedural Type Recovery
papers.description: NotDec lifts WebAssembly into SSA-based IR, uses Retypd-derived type constraints and pointer/value distinctions to recover structures, and emits C. Its study separates full interprocedural analysis from a faster intraprocedural variant.

papers.title: On the Viability of Requirements Generation from Code: An Experience Report
papers.description: Studies a RAG-based, human-supervised pipeline for recovering requirements and code traces from two projects. It also tests deliberate generation of unimplemented requirements and requirements smells (potential quality issues), exposing verification and labeling difficulties.

papers.title: POZZER: A Power Side Channel-guided Fuzzer for Black-Box Embedded Systems
papers.description: Builds a noise-tolerant pseudo execution-flow graph from one power trace per test input, using newly observed behavior as LibAFL feedback. It explores embedded firmware without access to its binary, source or instrumentation.

papers.title: PrismaCoder: Pushing the Boundaries of Open Multimodal Code Intelligence through Decomposed Rubric Synthesis
papers.description: Trains visual-code models using separate code and rendered-output rubrics for data filtering and reinforcement learning. Relevant evaluations include rebuilding webpages, charts and vector graphics from images.

papers.title: ProgramBench: Can Language Models Rebuild Programs From Scratch?
papers.description: Evaluates black-box program reconstruction across 200 tasks: agents query an executable and read its documentation, then independently implement a codebase whose behavior is checked by generated tests.

papers.title: ProgramDistill: From Interactive Web Apps to Verifiable Reference-Guided SWE Tasks
papers.description: Evaluates recovery of web-app behavior from a live reference with hidden source. It provides 4,063 feature-restoration tasks across 26 applications and a separate 12-application reconstruction setting, scored by replaying dependent browser workflows.

papers.title: Protocol Reverse Engineering via Deep Transfer Learning
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering / FSE 2026
papers.description: Transfers field-boundary patterns from standardized protocol traces labeled by Tshark to poorly documented target protocols. A source-selection stage chooses related protocols, and a neural domain-adaptation model infers message syntax from their shared patterns.

papers.title: Reactive Peripheral Modeling for Faithful Firmware Rehosting
papers.description: Bluezz models peripherals as stateful event-condition-action systems, coordinating interrupts, MMIO and DMA rather than treating accesses independently. It uses these models to rehost BLE firmware and reach connected protocol states for analysis and fuzzing.

papers.title: Recall-Oriented Precise Binary-to-Source Function Matching
papers.description: BScout matches decompiled functions to a source corpus using chunked embeddings and inlining-aware training. Existing matches provide positional clues to expand candidates; LLM selection and structural filters refine the resulting correspondences.

papers.title: Recovering Process Variables from Industrial Network Traffic via Search-Based Optimization
papers.description: PVParser recovers process-variable layouts from industrial traffic and historian records. Periodic-pattern detection locates relevant payloads; a modified Monte Carlo tree search proposes field boundaries, types and endianness, then aligns decoded sequences with observed process variables.

papers.title: RevengeBench: Reverse Engineering Code-Space Policies from Behavioral Experiments
papers.description: Tests whether agents can recover executable decision policies from behavioral traces and self-designed opponent probes, using 75 synthetic policies across five game arenas and measuring held-out action agreement and downstream competitive value.

papers.title: Reveree: Diagnosing LLM Reverse-Engineering Agents
papers.description: Evaluates reverse-engineering agent traces through flag recovery, eight analysis milestones and action profiles. Deterministic checks and an outcome-blinded LLM judge help locate failures beyond a single solve-rate score.

papers.title: RFCLLM: Evaluating LLMs' Reasoning Ability of Network Protocol State Machines
papers.description: Tests reasoning over protocol state machines using 1,482 questions across 16 protocols. Four context settings distinguish RFC retrieval from reasoning over supplied transitions; tasks cover next states, conditions, predecessor states and paths.

papers.title: SatBleed: Security of Commoditized Communication Modules in Satellites
papers.description: Studies satellite communication modules through hardware inspection, firmware reverse engineering, protocol analysis, partial rehosting and targeted testing. A component-level threat model connects recovered data flows to security boundaries.

papers.title: SCDBench: A Benchmark for LLM-Based Smart Contract Decompilers
papers.description: Benchmarks LLM-based EVM decompilation on 600 source-verified Ethereum Solidity contracts, sampled in easy, medium and hard thirds from 772,736 unique bytecode–source pairs after near-duplicate filtering. Each task supplies EVM assembly and optional four-byte selector hints and asks for self-contained Solidity with compiler settings. Outputs are scored in four cumulative stages: format completeness, compilation, ABI recovery, and semantic consistency, where 227,383 recorded test cases for 14,553 public functions are replayed on the recompiled output. With one compiler-feedback repair call, GPT-5.3-Codex compiled 90.3% of contracts, while the best semantic results were 29.4% of functions and 42 of 600 contracts recovered perfectly, both by Claude Opus 4.7.

papers.title: Schema: Discovering Unknown Environments via Agentic Program Induction
papers.description: Infers executable models of game state and transition rules from interaction. Agents revise these models against recorded history, search within them, and compare predicted observations with real outcomes while executing plans.

papers.title: ScreenCoder: Advancing Visual-to-Code Generation for Front-End Automation via Modular Multimodal Agents
papers.description: Splits screenshot-to-code generation among grounding, planning and generation agents that label UI regions, build a hierarchical layout tree and write HTML/CSS. The pipeline also produces the Screen-10K training pairs used for supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning, and the paper introduces the 1,000-page ScreenBench.

papers.title: Semantic Validation of Packer Identification Tools: Characterization, Repair, and Downstream Impact
papers.description: Uses unpacking outcomes as reference evidence to assess packer labels, normalizes heterogeneous tool results, and evaluates complementary signature/heuristic pools with static predicates derived from unpacker implementations. It traces how identification errors affect later unpacking and malware classification.

papers.title: ShieldedCode: Learning Robust Representations for Virtual Machine Protected Code
papers.description: ShieldedCode studies software protection from the defender's side: it trains code language models on pairs of C source functions and their virtualization-protected (VMP) x86-64 code so that the models can generate, compare and rank protected variants. Training pairs come from AnghaBench functions compiled at O0–O3, protected at levels L0–L3 by a commercial VMP tool, then disassembled and normalized. The model adds attention masks for dependencies within, between adjacent and across virtual instructions, contrastive objectives for functional equivalence and protection strength, and a protection-effectiveness task that ranks variants of the same source. Continual pre-training starts from CodeLlama 34B and adds The Stack to the corpus, and fine-tuning uses 2.5 million source–VM pairs. On HumanEval-compile, VM code generation reaches 26.95% Pass@1 at level L0 (GPT-4o: 22.58%) and 14.71% at L3. On BinaryCorp-VirtualAssembly similarity detection, Recall@1 for the O0+L1 setting is 0.488, against 0.333 for jTrans with a linear probe. The authors also run a manual reverse-engineering study and pattern-matching and angr attacks on the generated protection.

papers.title: SK2Decompile: LLM-based Two-Phase Binary Decompilation from Skeleton to Skin
papers.description: Splits LLM decompilation into two phases: a Structure Recovery model turns decompiler pseudocode into an identifier-free IR that keeps control flow and data structures, trained with compiler-based RL rewards, and an Identifier Naming model then restores names under a semantic-similarity reward. The authors report a 21.6% average re-executability gain over GPT-5-mini on HumanEval and a 29.4% average R2I improvement over Idioms on GitHub2025.

papers.title: SoK: A Large-Scale Empirical Study of Emulation-Based Dynamic Analysis Research for ARM Cortex-M Firmware (Extended Version)
papers.description: Organizes 24 MCU analysis tools into configuration recovery, emulation, fuzzing and diagnosis stages, then evaluates the runnable, pipeline-compatible subset on 4,571 filtered Cortex-M firmware images. Studies where recovered configurations and emulation artifacts fail to support later analysis.

papers.title: SoK: AI-Augmented Binary Reversing
papers.description: A systematization-of-knowledge survey of machine-learning, LLM and agentic approaches to binary reversing. Version 2 collects 246 papers published since 2015, found through keyword searches of 11 security, software-engineering and AI venues plus citation snowballing, and organizes them into 22 domains by inference task: from code-boundary detection and recovery of function names, types and struct layouts to code similarity, malware and vulnerability analysis, and decompilation. Its taxonomy links conventional triage, static, dynamic and security-testing analyses to AI pipelines through the binary-derived artifacts they exchange, and it derives 12 insights and open directions such as binary-aligned ground truth and goal-driven agentic reversing.

papers.title: SoK: Are LLMs Reliable at Source Code Recovery? A Taxonomy and Empirical Evaluation
papers.description: This SoK organizes LLM-assisted source-recovery designs and separates compilation, readability, structural and behavioral metrics. Its controlled study varies architecture, compiler optimization and symbol availability, with smaller ablations for input representation, model roles and source language.

papers.title: SPRITE: From Static Mockups to Engine-Ready Game UI
papers.description: Transforms game-interface screenshots into editable engine assets through hierarchical YAML, visual grounding, asset extraction, and Unity UXML/USS synthesis, with evaluation on a curated game-UI benchmark and review by three senior UI/UX designers.

papers.title: Stage-Supervised Latent Reasoning for Single-Shot JavaScript Deobfuscation
papers.description: Uses intermediate Webcrack rewrites to supervise Coconut-style latent reasoning for JavaScript deobfuscation. Training exposes staged code transformations; inference receives obfuscated code and generates a cleaned program in one shot.

papers.title: State-Aware Generation of Deployable Websites from Visual Prototypes and Requirements
papers.description: VisStateCoder links visual prototype elements, project files, interaction requirements and render evidence in a project state graph, then uses those links to generate websites and limit subsequent repairs to selected files.

papers.title: STILL: Recovering Lowered STL Semantics for LLM-assisted C++ Decompilation
papers.description: STILL predicts function-level STL container presence from stripped control-flow graphs and turns those predictions into compact hints for LLM refinement of Ghidra output. StlBench supplies controlled labels for five container classes.

papers.title: SWE-Game: Can Coding Agents Build the Games We Want?
papers.description: Evaluates construction, completion, repair and Godot-to-Unity porting against executable reference games. Evaluator-owned probes and input replays check gameplay behavior, while visual rubrics assess presentation separately.

papers.title: TaoD2C-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Industrial UI Code Generation Beyond Visual Fidelity
papers.description: TaoD2C-Bench reconstructs interfaces from design images, layer metadata and component-library documentation. It separates requirement inference from implementation, checking component choices and layout relations through source/runtime evidence alongside rendered appearance.

papers.title: The CodeInverter Suite: Structure- and Data-Aware Binary Decompilation with Efficient LLMs
papers.description: CodeInverter studies function-level LLM decompilation using control-flow graphs and memory-to-data mappings extracted with IDA/objdump. It presents a prompt workflow, training corpus and model family, evaluated through compilation, benchmark input/output tests and edit similarity.

papers.title: The Deception Delta: Adversarial Evaluation of LLM-Based Smart Contract Bytecode Forensics
papers.description: Evaluates how language models interpret raw EVM bytecode from purpose-built deceptive and control contracts. It distinguishes recognizing a hidden transfer mechanism from correctly judging its risk, using model judges alongside judge-independent checks.

papers.title: The Evolution of Binary Decompilation in the Modern Era: A Taxonomy, Literature Review, and Future Perspectives
papers.description: This survey maps traditional, dynamic, matching and neural decompilation approaches, then organizes type recovery, control-flow restructuring, naming and refinement tasks alongside evaluation metrics and benchmark choices. An accompanying repository provides the reviewed literature list.

papers.title: The Next Challenge for Agentic Cybersecurity: A Realistic, Contamination-Free Reverse Engineering Benchmark
papers.description: Introduces SRE-Bench, with privately authored programs and protected binary variants, to study agent recovery of program semantics while reducing training-data contamination.

papers.title: Towards LLM-Resistant Software Protection: Agent Failure Patterns in CTF Reverse Engineering
papers.description: Runs Claude Code, Codex CLI and ChatGPT-5.2 Pro on 24 crackme-style challenges selected from 15 international CTF events held in 2025, and attributes their failures to stages of an Observe–Comprehend–Plan loop and to three protection effects: concealment, complication and misdirection. From the failure logs, the authors derive four recurring weaknesses (training bias, over-trust in observations, context limitation and plan persistence). They rerun both CLI agents without a decompiler and compare outcomes with in-competition solve rates.

papers.title: Training Language Model Agents to Find Vulnerabilities with CTF-Dojo
papers.description: CTF-Dojo is an execution environment for training LLM agents on capture-the-flag tasks: 658 challenges from 50 competitions held between 2011 and 2025, taken from pwn.college's CTF Archive and containerized with Docker. Its CTF-Forge pipeline prompts DeepSeek-V3-0324 to write each challenge's Dockerfile, docker-compose file and challenge metadata; across three independent runs, 650 challenges consistently built and answered on their expected ports. Qwen3-Coder and DeepSeek-V3-0324 agents in the EnIGMA+ scaffold, capped at 40 turns, collected trajectories. Matched CTFtime writeups served as hints during collection and were removed afterwards, and ports, paths, distractor code and other runtime details were randomized per rollout. Rejection-sampling fine-tuning of Qwen3 8B, 14B and 32B on 486 flag-capturing trajectories from 274 solved challenges raises average Pass@1 on InterCode-CTF, NYU CTF Bench and Cybench by up to 11.6 points; the 32B model reaches 31.9%.

papers.title: Tycho: Active Abstraction with Programmatic World Models for ARC-AGI-3
papers.description: Tycho constructs editable Python models of game state, transitions, rendering and outcomes from action/observation histories in unfamiliar ARC-AGI-3 games. It checks model predictions against recorded transitions and can use, repair or bypass these models during planning.

papers.title: UI2App: Benchmarking Visual Interaction Inference in Executable Web Application Generation
papers.description: UI2App evaluates runnable React/TypeScript applications generated from 600 screenshots across 95 web applications. It separates build executability, visual fidelity and screenshot-implied interaction behavior, including cross-route state, using a reference interaction taxonomy and public evaluation pipeline.

papers.title: UniCoder: Unified Visual-to-Code Generation via Symbolic Rewards and Reference-Guided Code Optimization
papers.description: UniCoder trains a visual-to-code model for charts, SVGs and webpages. Its reinforcement-learning objective combines rendering checks, image similarity and code-derived visual attributes; low-reward training groups receive reference-code trajectories to improve exploration.

papers.title: User-Space Dependency-Aware Rehosting for Linux-Based Firmware Binaries
papers.description: FIRMWELL reconstructs the execution environment of Linux firmware services by running their initialization processes, locating blocking dependencies and repairing missing system-level behavior. It combines containerized QEMU-user emulation with a QEMU-system fallback, using process traces and binary analysis to recover resources needed by the target service.

papers.title: Vision2Web: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
papers.description: Benchmarks website development from visual prototypes and written requirements across 100 static-page, 66 interactive-frontend and 27 full-stack tasks, combining workflow-based functional checks with model-judged visual comparison.

papers.title: WebWorld: The Browser as a World Model for Self-Improving Web Code
papers.description: Uses typed browser interaction contracts to check progress and preserve previously verified capabilities while improving generated web code. Only accepted transitions become training examples.

papers.title: When LLM Decompilers Recompile More and Preserve Less
papers.description: Decompile-Diverge builds function-level behavioral comparisons from source-derived drivers and fuzzed reference inputs. The study compares reconstructed functions on the same inputs and examines divergences and missing crashes that compilation and supplied tests can miss.

papers.title: Beyond Classification: Inferring Function Names in Stripped Binaries via Domain Adapted LLMs
papers.description: SymGen infers function names for stripped binaries by generating them with a LoRA-fine-tuned Code Llama model instead of classifying over a fixed name vocabulary. Ghidra decompiles each stripped function, its own name is masked, and callee names are normalized for deduplication. Before fine-tuning, the model is domain-adapted on decompiled code paired with LLM-generated summaries of the matching source functions. On functions from 33 C projects built for x86-64, x86-32, ARM and MIPS at O0–O3, deduplicated from 2,237,915 to 495,494, the authors report average word-level F1 of 0.277 (0.380 on x86-64), plus case studies on obfuscated binaries and Linux malware.

papers.title: BinMetric: A Comprehensive Binary Code Analysis Benchmark for Large Language Models
papers.description: BinMetric poses 1,000 questions across six binary-analysis tasks: call-site reconstruction, decompilation, signature recovery, binary code summarization, algorithm classification and assembly instruction generation. The questions come from 20 open-source C projects compiled for x86-64, stripped and processed with IDA Pro, and aligned with source code through DWARF information. The authors evaluate 12 LLMs from five model families with one-shot prompts, alongside IDA Pro’s decompiler, LLM4Decompile, BinT5 and HexT5 where those apply.

papers.title: Cybench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities and Risks of Language Models
papers.description: Cybench turns 40 professional-level capture-the-flag tasks from four competitions (HackTheBox Cyber Apocalypse 2024, SekaiCTF 2022–23, GlacierCTF and HKCert) into runnable agent tasks. Each task has a description, starter files, a Kali Linux container for the agent with task servers in Docker, and the time the first human team needed to solve it, from 2 minutes to 24 hours 54 minutes. Each task is also split into subtasks that grade intermediate steps. The authors evaluate eight models with a structured bash agent and compare four scaffolds for GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Without subtask guidance, the best agents solved only tasks whose first human solve took at most 11 minutes, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet reached 17.5% unguided success.

papers.title: D-LiFT: Improving LLM-based Decompiler Backend via Code Quality-driven Fine-tuning
papers.description: D-LIFT uses D-Score to guide LLM fine-tuning and output selection, improving decompiled code while prioritizing accuracy. It evaluates Ghidra output from coreutils and util-linux.

papers.title: DeclarUI: Bridging Design and Development with Automated Declarative UI Code Generation
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE 2025)
papers.description: Combines visual component extraction, multimodal models, page-transition graphs and iterative checks to reconstruct multi-page mobile UI code from designs or screenshots, evaluated with React Native, Flutter and ArkUI.

papers.title: DecLLM: LLM-Augmented Recompilable Decompilation for Enabling Programmatic Use of Decompiled Code
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (ISSTA 2025)
papers.description: DecLLM repairs decompiler pseudocode that does not recompile into C that compiles and runs, so source-level tools such as CodeQL can be applied to binaries. An iterative loop feeds compiler errors to an off-the-shelf LLM, reverting illegal outputs and large deletions, then uses mismatched test outputs and AddressSanitizer reports from the rebuilt program to repair behavior, and finally fuzzes the original and rebuilt executables for divergences. With GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 the authors report 74% and 78.3% success on 300 Code Contest programs; on Coreutils and CGC binaries, 61.9–70.9% recompile and 48.1–59.0% are fully functional.

papers.title: Decompile-Bench: Million-Scale Binary-Source Function Pairs for Real-World Binary Decompilation
papers.description: Introduces two million C/C++ binary-source function pairs using a Compile-Trace-Filter pipeline, with an evaluation suite spanning translated HumanEval/MBPP tasks and recent GitHub functions.

papers.title: DecompileBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Decompilers in Real-World Scenarios
papers.description: Evaluates traditional and LLM-based decompilers using functions from real programs, runtime behavioral checks, and an LLM-assisted assessment of analyst-facing code understandability.

papers.title: Decompiling Smart Contracts with a Large Language Model
papers.description: Converts Ethereum Virtual Machine bytecode into Solidity in two stages. Static analysis first lifts the bytecode into three-address code with recovered control flow; a Llama-3.2-3B model fine-tuned with LoRA on 238,446 TAC-to-Solidity function pairs then writes each function. On 9,731 held-out functions from verified Ethereum contracts, the authors report average semantic similarity of 0.82 to the original source, with 78.3% of functions above 0.8. An ablation compares the untuned base model on 663 functions, and case studies decompile an unverified Dx Protocol contract and an exploited MEV bot.

papers.title: Design2Code: Benchmarking Multimodal Code Generation for Automated Front-End Engineering
papers.description: Evaluates reconstruction of frontend code from webpage screenshots using real-world reference pages, visual-element and layout metrics, and human assessment.

papers.title: Diffusion Models Are Real-Time Game Engines
papers.description: GameNGen learns to simulate DOOM interactively with a diffusion model instead of game code. A PPO agent first plays the game in ViZDoom, and its recorded trajectories, from random to trained play, become the training data. Stable Diffusion v1.4 is then fine-tuned to predict the next frame from the last 64 frames and actions, with noise added to context frames to keep long autoregressive rollouts stable and a fine-tuned latent decoder for detail. With 4 sampling steps it runs at 20 frames per second on one TPU-v5. The authors report next-frame PSNR of 29.43 and human raters picking the real game in 58–60% of short clips.

papers.title: DiSCo: Towards Decompiling EVM Bytecode to Source Code using Large Language Models
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE 2025)
papers.description: DiSCo lifts Ethereum contract creation bytecode to Solidity source by prompting a frozen LLM, instead of emitting decompiler pseudocode. It abstracts control-flow paths into logic-invariant semantic units, recovers constructor logic by simulating creation bytecode captured from block execution, and infers stripped names with signature databases and a type-aware graph model. These units become natural-language descriptions plus coding specifications in the prompt. GPT-4 is the primary model; Llama 3 is also tested.

papers.title: Divide-and-Conquer: Generating UI Code from Screenshots
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE 2025)
papers.description: Recursively divides a webpage screenshot along visual separation lines, has a multimodal model generate HTML/CSS for each leaf segment, and assembles child code upward into the full page; evaluated with GPT-4o, Gemini and Claude models and a small developer study.

papers.title: EnIGMA: Interactive Tools Substantially Assist LM Agents in Finding Security Vulnerabilities
papers.description: EnIGMA extends SWE-agent for capture-the-flag challenges with interactive agent tools that keep a gdb debugging session or a pwntools server connection open across turns, alongside decompile and disassemble commands, an LM summarizer for long outputs, and category-specific demonstrations and guidelines. It is evaluated with four LMs on 390 challenges from NYU CTF, InterCode-CTF, Cybench and a HackTheBox set the authors collected. The paper ablates tools, summarizers and demonstrations, and analyzes solution leakage and “soliloquizing”, where the model writes its own observations instead of acting in the environment.

papers.title: Exploring the Potential of LLMs for Code Deobfuscation
papers.description: Studies LLMs as source-to-source deobfuscators for C functions protected with the Tigress obfuscator. Functions from ExeBench, with identifiers randomized, are obfuscated with five transformations: MBA arithmetic encoding, branch encoding, control-flow flattening, opaque predicates and argument randomization. Each model receives a whole obfuscated function and returns simplified C. DeepSeek Coder 6.7B and Code Llama 7B are fine-tuned on obfuscated–original pairs, GPT-4 is prompted, and Clang optimization at -O0 to -O3 serves as a compiler baseline. Simplification is scored with Halstead program length relative to the original and obfuscated code, syntactic correctness by compiling ExeBench wrappers and semantic correctness by ExeBench input/output samples. The fine-tuned models reduce complexity more than GPT-4 on every transformation and more than Clang except on arithmetic encoding and argument randomization, where Clang is on par. Trained on chains of up to five transformations, they keep stable scores on chains of six and seven, and the best model cuts Halstead program length by 89.21% on average in the hardest scenario. A test with randomized constants found one sample that reproduced memorized code.

papers.title: ICEPRE: ICS Protocol Reverse Engineering via Data-Driven Concolic Execution
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (ISSTA 2025)
papers.description: Infers message-field boundaries by following concrete message-guided paths through binary protocol parsers, then symbolically replaying them to extract byte-level data flow. It merges bytes using value-preserving operations and similar processing traces. For the 1,000-message datasets of four public ICS protocols, the authors report average boundary F1 of 0.76 and field perfection of 0.67.

papers.title: Interaction2Code: Benchmarking MLLM-based Interactive Webpage Code Generation from Interactive Prototyping
papers.description: Benchmarks reconstruction of interactive webpages from screenshots before and after an interaction. The final study covers 127 webpages and 374 interactions, comparing rendered appearance, automated interaction checks, and human usability judgments.

papers.title: Is This the Same Code? A Comprehensive Study of Decompilation Techniques for WebAssembly Binaries
papers.description: Measures how well existing WebAssembly decompilers recover C, with native-binary decompilers as the baseline. The same C programs are compiled with Emscripten to WebAssembly and with clang to native code, then decompiled by wasm2c, w2c2 and wasm-decompile or by Ghidra and RetDec. Correctness reuses 1,000 Csmith programs from DecFuzzer, recompiling the output and comparing its execution with the original; code-complexity metrics and AST similarity to the original source are measured on PolyBenchC and CHStone at -O0 to -O2. wasm2c passed all 1,000 correctness programs, against 649 for wasm-decompile, 818 for Ghidra and 775 for RetDec.

papers.title: JsDeObsBench: Measuring and Benchmarking LLMs for JavaScript Deobfuscation
papers.description: Builds an execution-verifiable JavaScript deobfuscation benchmark by applying seven JavaScript-Obfuscator transformations to Project CodeNet programs with test cases, then scores LLM and tool outputs for syntax, execution, code simplification and similarity to the original code.

papers.title: Lares: LLM-driven Code Slice Semantic Search for Patch Presence Testing
papers.description: Lares tests whether a known 1-day vulnerability fix is present in a target binary function without recompiling the project. Its inputs are the target binary, the project source and the patch commit diff. A patch-enhancement step adds data- and control-flow context from the source (via Tree-sitter and Joern) to patches with few changed statements. An LLM then locates the pseudocode slice in the IDA Pro decompilation of the target function that corresponds to each patch slice. Finally, matched slices are normalized into equations and checked for equivalence with the Z3 SMT solver, and the LLM judges the cases Z3 cannot model, deciding whether the function matches the pre-patch or the patched version. On 4,480 test cases from 73 CVEs in OpenSSL, FreeType, tcpdump and libxml2, compiled with GCC 9.4.0 and Clang 6 at O0–O3 for x86, x64 and ARM, the authors report an average F1 of 0.77 on x86 with Claude 3.5 Sonnet, against 0.67 for Robin and 0.68 for PS3, and F1 from 0.71 to 0.77 across five compiler–architecture settings.

papers.title: LaTCoder: Converting Webpage Design to Code with Layout-as-Thought
papers.description: LaTCoder converts webpage design images to HTML/CSS by making layout an explicit intermediate step. A rule-based divider recursively finds solid-colored horizontal or vertical lines that avoid OCR-detected text, then merges small regions into grid-aligned blocks. An MLLM writes code for each block with a chain-of-thought prompt. The blocks are then assembled by absolute positioning or by the MLLM, and a reference-free verifier combining MAE and CLIP picks the better result. The paper also introduces CC-HARD, 128 complex-layout pages manually sampled from Common Crawl.

papers.title: Malsight: Exploring Malicious Source Code and Benign Pseudocode for Iterative Binary Malware Summarization
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
papers.description: MALSIGHT writes natural-language summaries of stripped binary malware one function at a time. IDA Pro produces pseudocode and a call graph, and functions are summarized callees first, so each caller receives its callees' summaries as context; a sequence-labeling model also marks key API calls and strings, which drive code-search retrieval and LLM-written annotations. The summarizer, MalT5, is a 0.77B-parameter CodeT5+ model fine-tuned first on MalS, 89,609 malicious C source functions from GitHub with LLM-generated summaries refined by human reviewers, and then on annotated benign pseudocode from the Capybara dataset. The authors also introduce MalP, 500 pseudocode functions for testing, and BLEURT-sum, a fine-tuned BLEURT metric, and report that MalT5 performs comparably to much larger Code Llama models.

papers.title: Nova: Generative Language Models for Assembly Code with Hierarchical Attention and Contrastive Learning
papers.description: Nova is a generative LLM for x86-64 assembly, trained from DeepSeek-Coder checkpoints on stripped, normalized gcc -O0 to -O3 assembly built from AnghaBench and The Stack. It adds hierarchical attention that builds per-instruction summaries, and contrastive objectives that keep a function's source and O0–O3 assembly close while ordering them by optimization level. Fine-tuned for decompilation, Nova-1.3B and Nova-6.7B reach 25.17% and 34.36% average Pass@1 on HumanEval-Decompile, 14.84 and 12.41 points above same-size LLM4Decompile; separately fine-tuned models report the highest average Recall@1 for O0-to-O3 binary code similarity on six real-world projects.

papers.title: On Benchmarking Code LLMs for Android Malware Analysis
papers.description: CAMA is a framework for benchmarking how code LLMs read decompiled Android malware. Androguard decompiles each APK into Java functions, and each model returns a structured output per function: a summary, a refined function name and a 0–10 maliciousness score. Two analysis tasks build on these outputs. Malicious-function identification is scored by consistency (whether scores and names stay stable when the model is re-prompted with its own summaries) and by fidelity (how much a LightGBM malware-category classifier loses confidence when the top-scored function descriptors are removed). Malware-purpose summarization is scored by semantic relevance (BLEU, METEOR and ROUGE-L against reference app descriptions). The benchmark holds 118 APKs from 6 categories and 13 families, with 7,542,799 decompiled functions. Of the four models evaluated, StarChat-Beta has the highest maliciousness consistency (0.813, against 0.381 for CodeLlama) and narrowly the highest semantic-relevance scores, while fidelity varies widely across models and removal sizes. Renaming functions with model-suggested names raises fidelity for CodeLlama and StarChat but lowers METEOR by about 10%.

papers.title: PoE-World: Compositional World Modeling with Products of Programmatic Experts
papers.description: PoE-World represents an Atari world model as an exponentially weighted product of many small Python programs, or programmatic experts, each synthesized by an LLM to explain one aspect of the observed dynamics; learned weights and optional synthesized hard constraints combine them. From object lists that OCAtari parses out of a demonstration of fewer than 1,000 frames, the authors learn stochastic, partially observed models of Pong and Montezuma's Revenge and use them in a planning agent, including on rearranged Pong-Alt and Montezuma's Revenge-Alt variants that have no demonstrations.

papers.title: ReF Decompile: Relabeling and Function Call Enhanced Decompile
papers.description: ReF Decompile relabels jump targets and uses function calls to recover variable information when converting binary code to source code. It was evaluated on the HumanEval-Decompile Benchmark.

papers.title: REx86: A Local Large Language Model for Assisting in x86 Assembly Reverse Engineering
papers.venue: 2025 IEEE Annual Computer Security Applications Conference (ACSAC)
papers.description: The paper fine-tunes eight local models from CodeLlama, Qwen2.5-Coder, and CodeGemma on 5,981 x86 assembly examples and evaluates their help with binary reverse engineering.

papers.title: Sketch2Code: Evaluating Vision-Language Models for Interactive Web Design Prototyping
papers.description: Sketch2Code benchmarks vision-language models on turning rough hand-drawn wireframe sketches into HTML webpage prototypes. Crowd annotators drew 731 sketches of 484 real-world webpages from the Design2Code test set. Ten models, eight commercial and two 8B open-source, generate pages directly and in two multi-turn settings with a GPT-4o simulated user: following its feedback, or asking it clarification questions. Outputs are scored by Design2Code visual similarity and a new IoU-based layout similarity over component types such as text blocks, images, navigation bars, forms and buttons. Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o lead single-turn layout similarity, and feedback rounds help commercial models more than question asking does.

papers.title: StructEval: Benchmarking LLMs' Capabilities to Generate Structural Outputs
papers.description: Evaluates generation and conversion of structured outputs, including HTML, React and SVG, with separate checks for format adherence and structural correctness.

papers.title: Target-Centric Firmware Rehosting with Penguin
papers.description: Penguin rehosts embedded Linux firmware from an extracted filesystem by deriving an editable configuration of emulation transformations, such as file changes, pseudofiles, NVRAM values and network interfaces, from static analysis. Dynamic-analysis plugins expose failures so the configuration can be refined for each target, and a minimizer identifies which transformations a working rehosting needs.

papers.title: TypeForge: Synthesizing and Selecting Best-Fit Composite Data Types for Stripped Binaries
papers.description: TypeForge recovers composite data types, including struct layouts, unions and pointer or nesting relationships, from stripped binaries. A whole-program Type Flow Graph over Ghidra’s decompiler-inferred variables propagates member offsets and sizes, cuts conflicting edges caused by casts and unions, and synthesizes candidate type declarations. An LLM only selects among these statically synthesized candidates: each is applied through the decompiler’s retype interface, and a double-elimination tournament compares the resulting pseudocode for readability. On OSPREY’s coreutils dataset the authors report F1 of 81.7% for composite-type identification, 88.2% for layout recovery and 72.1% for relationship recovery.

papers.title: UIOrchestra: Generating High-Fidelity Code from UI Designs with a Multi-agent System
papers.description: UIOrchestra converts static mobile UI designs into React/CSS through layout-description, code-generation and rendered-image comparison agents. Its APPUI benchmark contains 1,101 human-refined code/rendering pairs based on screenshots from 165 apps across 12 categories. The reference code is reconstructed for evaluation, rather than recovered original application source.

papers.title: Unleashing the Power of Generative Model in Recovering Variable Names from Stripped Binary
papers.description: GenNm suggests names for placeholder variables in decompiled code of stripped binaries by fine-tuning generative code models (CodeGemma-2B by default; CodeLlama-7B and a LoRA-tuned CodeLlama-34B are also tested). Queries add renamed caller code and callee signatures propagated along the call graph; a DPO-style symbol-preference optimization (SymPO) counters bias toward frequent training names, and a data-flow name-validation step chooses among candidates over iterative rounds. The authors report 5.6–11.4-point precision gains over VarBERT and ReSym on rebuilt DIRTY and VarCorpus datasets, and 22.8% precision on names unseen in training against 17.3% for the strongest baseline.

papers.title: Unleashing the Power of LLM to Infer State Machine From the Protocol Implementation
papers.description: ProtocolGPT infers protocol state machines from implementation source code with a retrieval-augmented LLM. It extracts state-machine-related code with regular expressions and a code filter, splits it into syntax-aware chunks stored in a FAISS vector store with OpenAI embeddings, and prompts GPT-4 step by step to recover states and message-triggered transitions. On six protocols in five open-source code bases (IKEv2, TLS 1.3, TLS 1.2, BGP, RTSP and L2TP), the authors report transition precision above 90%, more than 30% higher precision and 55% higher recall than baselines. Seeding AFLNet with the inferred machines raised coverage by more than 20% and found two previously unknown crash bugs in an RTSP server.

papers.title: WAFFLE: Fine-tuning Multi-Modal Model for Automated Front-End Development
papers.description: WAFFLE fine-tunes multimodal LLMs to generate HTML/CSS from UI screenshots. A quarter of the decoder's attention heads use a structure-aware mask that limits each element's tokens to its parent, preceding siblings and its own earlier tokens. A contrastive objective aligns image and code embeddings over groups of four mutated WebSight-v0.1 pages. With VLM-WebSight and Moondream2 backbones, the authors report up to 9.00 pp higher HTML-Match and 0.0982 higher CW-SSIM than standard fine-tuning on WebSight-Test, plus gains on every Design2Code metric.

papers.title: WebCode2M: A Real-World Dataset for Code Generation from Webpage Designs
papers.description: WebCode2M pairs about 2.56 million real-world webpage screenshots with purified HTML/CSS code and element bounding-box layout trees. Pages sampled from a Common Crawl snapshot are cleaned (scripts, metadata and hidden elements removed, styles merged into one block), rendered with Playwright, and filtered by a neural scorer trained on 10,000 annotated samples. The paper fine-tunes Pix2Struct-1.3B as the WebCoder baseline, introduces TreeBLEU to measure DOM-structure recall, and benchmarks specialized, open and commercial multimodal models on short, medium and long test subsets of 256 pages each.

papers.title: WebUIBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models in WebUI-to-Code
papers.description: Diagnoses webpage-to-code capability through visual perception, HTML programming, image-to-HTML understanding, and screenshot reconstruction tasks. It separates underlying skills using question-answer pairs derived from real websites.

papers.title: A Taxonomy of C Decompiler Fidelity Issues
papers.description: Open-codes decompiled/original C function pairs to classify how decompiler output departs from the source beyond missing names and types. Using a statement-alignment abstraction and thematic analysis, the authors build a hierarchical codebook of 15 top-level categories and 52 codes, covering correctness issues such as nonequivalent expressions and incorrect return behavior and readability issues such as extraneous variables, non-idiomatic control flow and decompiler-specific macros. The codebook, developed on Hex-Rays output, is applied to Ghidra, retdec and angr, and the authors suggest type prediction, rule-based fixes and whole-program learned techniques to address classes of defects.

papers.title: Assemblage: Automatic Binary Dataset Construction for Machine Learning
papers.description: Assemblage is a distributed system that crawls GitHub and vcpkg, builds C/C++ projects under many compiler configurations, and records source-to-binary mappings such as function addresses, source code, comments and PDB or DWARF debug information. Run on AWS for about a year, it produced 890k Windows PE binaries built with Visual Studio 2015–2022 across optimization levels, architectures and Debug/Release modes, plus 428k Linux ELF binaries from GCC and Clang, in 29 configurations. Case studies use the data for compiler provenance with PassTell, function similarity with a graph neural network and jTrans, and function-boundary identification comparing XDA with IDA.

papers.title: Assessing LLMs in Malicious Code Deobfuscation of Real-world Malware Campaigns
papers.description: The paper evaluates four LLMs on deobfuscating real-world malicious scripts from the Emotet malware campaign and examines their use in reverse engineering.

papers.title: BinaryAI: Binary Software Composition Analysis via Intelligent Binary Source Code Matching
papers.description: BinaryAI identifies which open-source C/C++ libraries a stripped binary reuses by matching its functions to source code. Ghidra decompiles each binary function to pseudo-C, and a Pythia-410M model, trained with a CLIP-style contrastive loss on about 10 million binary–source function pairs, embeds pseudo-code and source functions in one space. Candidates retrieved from a corpus of 56,342,179 source functions from 12,013 libraries are refined with link-time locality and the call graph, and a library is reported when the share of its matched functions exceeds a threshold. The authors report 22.54% recall@1 against 10.75% for CodeCMR, and library-detection precision and recall of 85.84% and 64.98% against 73.36% and 59.81% for an unnamed commercial tool.

papers.title: BinPRE: Enhancing Field Inference in Binary Analysis Based Protocol Reverse Engineering
papers.description: Infers protocol-message field boundaries and semantics from instrumented server binaries and input messages. BinPRE groups bytes by the instruction operators that process them, applies detectors for field types and functions, then refines results across similar messages. On eight protocols with 50 messages each, the authors report average field perfection of 0.73 and type/function F1 scores of 0.74/0.81.

papers.title: CEBin: A Cost-Effective Framework for Large-Scale Binary Code Similarity Detection
papers.description: CEBin combines code embeddings to shortlist candidate functions with pairwise comparison to detect similar binary code, including vulnerable functions.

papers.title: CLAP: Learning Transferable Binary Code Representations with Natural Language Supervision
papers.description: CLAP (Contrastive Language-Assembly Pre-training) learns assembly-function embeddings aligned with natural-language explanations. A dataset engine compiles Ubuntu C/C++ packages with GCC and Clang at O0–O3 and Os, has GPT-3.5 explain about 2.6 million matching source functions, and fine-tunes a Vicuna-13B “shadow model” on half of those explanations to label more code, yielding 195 million assembly–explanation pairs. A 110M-parameter assembly encoder, using address rebasing, a WordPiece tokenizer and jump-aware embeddings, is first pre-trained on assembly and then contrastively aligned with a text encoder. The embeddings support zero-shot classification by matching code against text prompts. On BinaryCorp-3M similarity search in pools of 10,000 functions, zero-shot CLAP reports 0.836 average recall@1 against 0.571 for fine-tuned jTrans.

papers.title: Code is not Natural Language: Unlock the Power of Semantics-Oriented Graph Representation for Binary Code Similarity Detection
papers.description: HermesSim detects binary code similarity by lifting each function to Ghidra P-code and building a semantics-oriented graph that exposes operand structure inside instructions, def-use, control-flow and effect-order relations, while dropping semantics-independent details such as which register temporarily holds a value. A gated graph neural network with a multi-head softmax aggregator embeds the graph, and functions are compared by embedding similarity. On the Dataset-1 benchmark of Marcelli et al., the authors report 48.1% RECALL@1 for x64 cross-compiler retrieval in pools of 10,000 functions, against 31.4% for a fine-tuned jTrans, with a 388K-parameter model.

papers.title: CodeArt: Better Code Models by Attention Regularization When Symbols Are Lacking
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering (FSE 2024)
papers.description: CodeArt pre-trains a BERT-sized encoder from scratch on 26 million stripped x86-64 functions built from jTrans's BinaryCorp. Instead of relying on symbols, it uses IDA Pro control-flow graphs and a binary data-flow analysis to compute control and data dependences, then restricts self-attention with masks so a token attends only to instructions it transitively depends on or that depend on it, to tokens in its own instruction, and to a global [CLS] token; pre-training masks tokens and perturbs the dependence graph. The authors fine-tune it for binary similarity, malware family classification and type inference. They report improvements over prior models from 53% to 64% recall@1 for similarity in pools of 500, from 49% to 60% LRAP for malware families, and from 74% to 94% average F1 for type inference.

papers.title: Cross-Inlining Binary Function Similarity Detection
papers.description: Studies binary function similarity when function inlining makes one binary function correspond to several source functions. From BinKit builds of 51 GNU projects with and without -fno-inline (9 GCC and Clang versions, O0–O3, six x86, ARM and MIPS targets; 216 combinations each), debug-line mappings label 5,621,140 cross-inlining pairs. The authors identify Leaf-, Root- and Internal-Inlining patterns, show that Gemini, SAFE and GMN lose accuracy on them, and propose CI-Detector, which trains one attributed-CFG graph neural network per pattern and aggregates their scores, reporting 81% precision and 97% recall.

papers.title: D-Helix: A Generic Decompiler Testing Framework Using Symbolic Differentiation
papers.description: Tests decompilers function by function on binaries without needing source code. RECOMPILER repairs decompiled C so individual functions recompile, SYMDIFF compares symbolic models of the original binary function and the recompiled decompiled function using patched angr and PROMPT symbolic executors, and TUNER toggles decompiler heuristic rules to locate, and sometimes work around, the rule behind an inaccuracy. On Ghidra 10.0 and angr 9.2.30, 2,004 binaries and object files from coreutils, util-linux and six popular GitHub C projects yield 93K decompiled functions; the authors report 4,515 incorrectly decompiled functions, 8 reproduced known bugs, 17 previously unknown bugs and 7 bugs fixed automatically.

papers.title: DeGPT: Optimizing Decompiler Output with LLM
papers.description: Refines existing C-like decompiler output through three coordinated roles that select, propose and check changes. It simplifies structures, adds comments and renames variables; Micro Snippet Semantic Calculation compares simulated symbol values and calls before accepting structural changes. The authors evaluate readability and naming on 620 functions from four codebases, with separate stripped and non-stripped variants.

papers.title: DynPRE: Protocol Reverse Engineering via Dynamic Inference
papers.description: DynPRE starts from captured client–server traces and then interacts with a live protocol server to infer message formats and types. It detects session-specific identifiers such as cookies and rewrites them on the fly so that replayed requests stay valid. It then sends byte-level probe requests whose responses serve as semantic feedback for field identification, aligns the responses, and applies a request–response mapping refinement that also recognizes message types. On 12 protocols with 10-, 100- and 1,000-message datasets, the authors report average field perfection of 0.50 and message-type V-measure of 0.94, against 0.15–0.31 perfection for Netzob, NetPlier, FieldHunter, BinaryInferno and NEMESYS.

papers.title: Exploring the Efficacy of Large Language Models (GPT-4) in Binary Reverse Engineering
papers.description: The paper evaluates GPT-4 for binary reverse engineering through interpretation of human-written and decompiled code, from basic code explanation to malware analysis.

papers.title: FoC: Figure out the Cryptographic Functions in Stripped Binaries with LLMs
papers.description: FoC uses FoC-BinLLM to summarize cryptographic functions in stripped binaries and FoC-Sim to retrieve similar implementations. It evaluates both models and applications to virus analysis and 1-day vulnerability detection.

papers.title: Generating Code World Models with Large Language Models Guided by Monte Carlo Tree Search
papers.description: GIF-MCTS generates executable Python transition and reward models from natural-language environment descriptions and offline state-transition trajectories, using prediction feedback to generate, improve and repair code. CWMB evaluates 18 reinforcement-learning environments and downstream planning; a separate experiment uses a simplified Read to Fight Monsters grid world.

papers.title: How Far Have We Gone in Binary Code Understanding Using Large Language Models
papers.description: Benchmarks 16 code and general LLMs on function name recovery and summarization of stripped binaries. The benchmark takes 12 popular C projects built for x86-64, strips and decompiles 28 binaries with IDA Pro, aligns 81,185 functions with source through DWARF, and keeps 2,000 functions after expert review. Zero-shot LLMs are compared with SymLM, NER, BinT5 and HexT5. Code Llama 34B leads name recovery with token-level F1 of 27.59, and ChatGPT leads summarization with BLEU-4 7.37. The study also measures few-shot prompting, LoRA fine-tuning of two 7B models on GNU binaries, and a case study on a stripped open-source Linux remote-access trojan.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Code Analysis: Do LLMs Really Do Their Job?
papers.description: Evaluates GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, LLaMA-2-13B, Code-LLaMA-2-13B-Instruct and StarChat-Beta on explaining what de-commented JavaScript, Python and C code does, then repeats the task on JavaScript obfuscated with JavaScript Obfuscator (identifier renaming, dead-code injection, control-flow flattening and string splitting) and with Wobfuscator’s WebAssembly transformation. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 are also asked to rewrite 100 IOCCC winning programs as readable, compilable code. Case studies apply GPT models to a botnet and a benign browser-extension repository, an Android SMS stealer decompiled with JD-GUI, and WannaCry code decompiled with RetDec.

papers.title: LLM4Decompile: Decompiling Binary Code with Large Language Models
papers.description: Trains language models for assembly-to-C decompilation and for refining Ghidra pseudocode, evaluating whether recovered functions can be recompiled and executed correctly.

papers.title: NYU CTF Bench: A Scalable Open-Source Benchmark Dataset for Evaluating LLMs in Offensive Security
papers.description: NYU CTF Bench packages 200 manually validated challenges from CSAW CTF qualifying and final rounds held between 2017 and 2023, spanning cryptography, forensics, pwn, reverse engineering, web and miscellaneous tasks, with challenge.json metadata and Docker images for server-side challenges. The paper also presents an automated framework that gives LLMs function-calling tools for shell commands, file creation, Ghidra disassembly and decompilation, flag checking and giving up. It evaluates five LLMs and compares their scores with human teams at CSAW 2022 and 2023.

papers.title: ReSym: Harnessing LLMs to Recover Variable and Data Structure Symbols from Stripped Binaries
papers.description: Combines two fine-tuned language models with Prolog-based cross-function reasoning to infer local-variable symbols and user-defined data structures from stripped-binary decompilation.

papers.title: Self-Constructed Context Decompilation with Fined-grained Alignment Enhancement
papers.description: Adds two techniques to LLM decompilation of function-level x86-64 GCC assembly into C. Self-Constructed Context Decompilation (sc²dec) recompiles a model’s first compilable output and uses the resulting assembly–source pair as an in-context example for a second attempt, without fine-tuning. Fine-grained Alignment Enhancement (FAE) fine-tunes llm4decompile-6.7b with LoRA on statement-level assembly–C alignments derived from DWARF debug information. Combining both, the authors report 52.41% average re-executability on Decompile-Eval, against 48.60% for the base model.

papers.title: SLaDe: A Portable Small Language Model Decompiler for Optimized Assembly
papers.description: SLaDe translates function-level assembly into C with a 200M-parameter encoder–decoder model, code-specific tokenization and PsycheC type completion. It studies x86 and ARM at -O0 and -O3, combining generated candidates with input/output checks. The input is assembly text, not raw machine bytes; disassembly is outside the method.

papers.title: StackSight: Unveiling WebAssembly through Large Language Models and Neurosymbolic Chain-of-Thought Decompilation
papers.description: StackSight decompiles WebAssembly text-format functions into C++ with LLM prompting. A static analysis annotates each WAT instruction with the virtual-stack state, using symbolic notation where branches diverge; a one-shot chain-of-thought prompt then asks the model to recover variable meanings, summarize the function and write C++. With GPT-4 the share of outputs passing all benchmark tests rises from 19.7% to 36.5% on HumanEval-X and from 42.4% to 59.6% on MBXP relative to one-shot prompting; GPT-3.5 and Code Llama-7B-Instruct are also evaluated.

papers.title: STRIDE: Simple Type Recognition In Decompiled Executables
papers.description: STRIDE predicts the names and types of variables in decompiler output without a neural model. From training decompilation with known labels, it builds a database mapping the token sequences (N-grams, with N from 2 to 60) immediately left and right of each variable occurrence to the five most frequent names or types. Variable placeholders are canonicalized, and address-like tokens and large constants are bucketed so that N-grams can match. At prediction time it looks up the longest matching N-gram on each side of every occurrence, scores the returned labels by how specific the match is, and sums the scores across the function. The prototype is about 1,000 lines of Python and runs on a CPU. On DIRT functions not seen in training, the authors report 66.4% retyping accuracy, against 52.3% for DIRTY with beam search, and 56.2% renaming accuracy, against 51.3% reported for VarBERT. Across 16 VarCorpus splits, renaming accuracy is higher than VarBERT on 11 and 1.55 points higher on average. Prediction takes 8.2 ms per function on a CPU, against 43.7 ms for VarBERT on an NVIDIA L4 GPU.

papers.title: TYGR: Type Inference on Stripped Binaries using Graph Neural Networks
papers.description: TYGR infers the types of stack and heap variables in stripped binaries by running an architecture-agnostic, intra-procedural data-flow analysis on angr's VEX IR and classifying each variable's data-flow graph with a graph neural network. It predicts base types, pointers and struct member layouts, covering 97.1% of the types observed in its data. The authors also build TyDa, 163,643 binaries compiled with debug information from Gentoo and Debian C packages for x86, x64, AArch64, Arm32 and MIPS at O0–O3, and deduplicate functions in the evaluated subset before splitting it. On x64 across O0–O3 they report 76.6% overall and 45.2% struct accuracy, and say TYGR beats prior work by at least 26.1% overall and 10.2% on structs.

papers.title: Unlocking the conversion of Web Screenshots into HTML Code with the WebSight Dataset
papers.description: WebSight is a synthetic dataset of 2 million HTML documents paired with full-page screenshots for training screenshot-to-HTML models. Mistral-7B-Instruct generates website concepts, Deepseek-Coder-33B-Instruct writes each page in HTML with Tailwind CSS, images come from keyword-based stock-photo URLs, and Playwright renders the screenshots after filtering. This v0.2 release replaces the 823K-pair v0.1, which used traditional CSS and colored rectangles instead of images. The authors fine-tune an 8B vision-language model, Sightseer, on the data with DoRA and show qualitative conversions, including one from a hand-drawn sketch.

papers.title: WaDec: Decompiling WebAssembly Using Large Language Model
papers.description: WaDec decompiles WebAssembly text (wat) into C by fine-tuning CodeLlama-7b with LoRA on loop-level wat–C snippet pairs. Functions are ordered by dependency and sliced so that each input holds at most one loop, with nested loops replaced by markers.
